commands.name: ls
commands.description: Lists files and folders in the current or a specified directory.

options.description: Show detailed information: permissions, ownership, size, and date.
Include hidden entries beginning with a dot.
Show human-readable file sizes, useful with -l.
Colorize entries automatically on GNU ls.

examples.description: Show details, hidden entries, and readable sizes.

commands.note: Combine short flags: ls -la is equivalent to ls -l -a. Available options can differ by system.

commands.name: cd
commands.description: Changes the Bash shell's current working directory.

options.description: Parent directory (an argument, not a flag).
Go to the previous directory (an argument, not a flag).

examples.description: Go to Documents in your home directory.

commands.note: cd changes your shell's location, not the location of files.

commands.name: pwd
commands.description: Prints the full path to the directory you are currently in.

options.description: Show the logical path, which may contain symbolic links.
Resolve symbolic links and print the physical path.

commands.name: mkdir
commands.description: Creates one or more directories at the specified paths.

options.description: Create missing parent directories; allow directories that already exist.
Print a message for each newly created directory.

examples.description: Create nested directories, including missing parents.

commands.name: touch
commands.summary: Create empty files or update timestamps
commands.description: Updates file access and modification timestamps; by default creates missing files.

examples.description: Create an empty file if needed.
Update timestamps only if the file exists.

commands.name: cp
commands.description: Copies files and, with an option, entire directories.

options.description: Avoid overwriting destinations when supported; behavior varies.

examples.description: Copy a directory and request confirmation before overwriting.

commands.note: Some flags differ between GNU and BSD implementations.

commands.name: mv
commands.description: Moves files and folders or changes their names.

options.description: Avoid overwriting an existing target when supported.
Show the entries that were moved.

examples.description: Move a file into another directory.
Ask before replacing an existing file.

commands.note: A destination file may be replaced without warning unless protective options are used.

commands.name: rm
commands.description: Deletes files, typically without moving them to Trash or Recycle Bin.

options.description: Ask for confirmation before each deletion.
Delete directories and their contents recursively; use caution.

commands.note: Warning: rm deletions are usually difficult to undo. Check paths carefully and consider -i.

commands.name: cat
commands.description: Prints the contents of files to the terminal; suitable for relatively short files.

options.description: Collapse repeated empty lines when supported.

examples.description: Show a file with line numbers.

commands.note: Use less to browse long files.

commands.name: sort
commands.description: Sorts lines from files or standard input, using locale-specific ordering by default.

options.description: Sort using field N as the key.
Write sorted output to the specified file.

examples.description: Sort simple CSV data by the second field.

commands.note: Use -nr together for reverse numeric order.

commands.name: grep
commands.description: Searches text or regular expressions and prints matching lines.

options.description: Print lines that do not match.
Treat the pattern as literal text.

commands.note: Quote patterns containing spaces. Use -F for plain-text matching.

commands.name: find
commands.summary: Find files by name or properties
commands.description: Walks directory trees and selects files or directories matching an expression.

options.description: Match filenames with a glob; quote the pattern.
Match filenames without case sensitivity when supported.
Limit recursion depth on GNU find.

examples.description: Find .txt files under the current directory.
Find files whose names begin with report.

commands.note: Quote *.txt so Bash does not expand the pattern before find receives it.

commands.name: head
commands.summary: Display the beginning of a file
commands.description: Shows the first ten lines of a file by default.

commands.name: tail
commands.summary: Display the end of a file
commands.description: Shows the last ten lines of a file by default, optionally following additions.

options.description: Follow new lines as they are added.

examples.description: Follow a log file; press Ctrl+C to stop.

commands.name: wc
commands.description: Counts words, newline characters, bytes, or characters in files or input.

options.description: Count characters according to the locale.

examples.description: Show line, word, and byte counts.

commands.note: wc -l counts newline characters; a final line without a newline might not be counted.

commands.name: less
commands.description: Opens text in a scrollable pager instead of flooding the terminal.

options.description: Search for text inside less (not a flag).
Quit the pager (a key, not a flag).

examples.description: Browse a log with line numbers.

commands.note: Use arrows to scroll, / to search, and q to quit.

commands.name: echo
commands.description: Prints its arguments; echo is a Bash builtin.

options.description: Example of variable expansion; not a flag.

commands.note: For precise and portable formatting, consider printf.

commands.name: man
commands.description: Displays locally installed manual pages for commands.

options.description: Quit the manual viewer (not a flag).

examples.description: Search for commands related to copying.

commands.note: Manual pages may contain options beyond those in this quick reference.

commands.name: clear
commands.description: Clears the visible terminal screen.

commands.name: printf
commands.description: Prints data according to a format string, allowing control over line breaks and layout.

options.description: Newline escape inside a format string (not a flag).

examples.description: Print Hello followed by a newline.
Print a label and a number.

commands.note: Unlike echo, printf does not add a newline automatically.

commands.name: cut
commands.description: Selects fields or character ranges from each input line.
commands.note: cut is not a complete parser for complex quoted CSV files.

commands.name: uniq
commands.description: Collapses consecutive identical lines; sort input first to eliminate nonadjacent duplicates.

options.description: Show lines that appear only once.

commands.note: uniq does not sort; it only checks neighboring lines.

commands.name: tr
commands.description: Replaces, removes, or squeezes characters from standard input.

options.description: Map characters in SET1 to SET2 (arguments).

examples.description: Collapse repeated spaces in a file.

commands.note: tr works with characters rather than entire words.

commands.name: sed
commands.description: Processes text using editing expressions, such as displaying selected lines or replacing text.

options.description: Replace old with new throughout each line.

examples.description: Show only the first five lines.
Replace every occurrence of cat with dog.

commands.note: By default, sed outputs changes without modifying its source file. In-place options vary by system.

commands.name: awk
commands.description: Processes text records and fields with conditions, expressions, and simple calculations.

options.description: Refer to the first input field in awk.
Built-in variable for the current record number.

commands.note: In awk, $1 refers to the first field and $0 to the entire record; these are not Bash variables.

commands.name: tee
commands.description: Sends input to both the terminal and a file, commonly in a pipeline.

examples.description: Show text and save it to a file.
Append another line to an existing file.

commands.note: Without -a, tee may overwrite an existing file.

commands.name: xargs
commands.description: Constructs command-line arguments from values read through standard input.

options.description: Use no more than N arguments per invocation.
Read NUL-separated input for safe filename handling.
Replace a placeholder with each input value.

examples.description: Run echo once per input item.
Insert each input item into a command argument.

commands.note: Use NUL-separated input and xargs -0 for filenames containing spaces or newlines, when available.

commands.name: diff
commands.description: Shows differences between files without changing them.
commands.note: Exit status 0 means equal; 1 means differences were detected.

commands.name: chmod
commands.description: Changes read, write, and execute permissions for files and directories.

options.description: Add execute permission for selected classes.
Let the owner execute the file.

examples.description: Make a script executable by its owner.

commands.note: u means owner, g group, o others, and a everyone. Executable files are not necessarily safe.

commands.name: du
commands.description: Reports disk space occupied by files and directories.

options.description: Display only a total per path.
Include files as well as directories.

commands.note: Disk usage can differ from a file's apparent logical size.

commands.name: df
commands.description: Displays used and available capacity for mounted filesystems.

examples.description: Show free space for the current directory's filesystem.

commands.note: df measures filesystem space, whereas du measures usage by individual paths.

commands.name: file
commands.description: Examines file contents to infer their type independently of the filename extension.

options.description: Print the type without the filename.

examples.description: Show the type without the name.

commands.note: Content-based detection is useful, but not always definitive.

commands.name: type
commands.summary: Inspect how Bash resolves a command
commands.description: Shows whether a name is a builtin, alias, function, or executable.

options.description: Print a short classification such as builtin or file.
Find the executable in PATH, if available.

examples.description: Check whether ls is an alias or executable.

commands.note: type is a Bash builtin and can recognize functions and aliases.

commands.name: history
commands.description: Prints previous Bash commands that are retained in the session's history.

options.description: Show the most recent N entries (argument, not flag).
Clear the current session's in-memory history.

commands.note: History retention depends on shell settings.

commands.name: ps
commands.description: Displays information about active system processes.

options.description: Show BSD-style process listing without a dash.

examples.description: Show processes associated with your terminal.

commands.note: ps supports multiple flag styles; availability depends on the system.

commands.name: tar
commands.description: Bundles files into archives and can use compression such as gzip.

options.description: Use gzip compression or decompression when supported.

examples.description: List files in an archive without extracting.

commands.note: Inspect archives before extracting. Option ordering may determine which filename is used.

commands.name: date
commands.description: Prints the current date and time using default or custom formatting.
commands.note: Format strings start with +; tokens such as %Y and %m represent date components.

commands.name: basename
commands.description: Returns the last component of a path without preceding directories.

options.description: Optional suffix to remove (argument, not flag).
Mark the end of options, where supported.

commands.note: basename works on text paths and does not require the file to exist.

commands.name: dirname
commands.description: Returns the directory component of a path, omitting its last component.

options.description: Mark the end of options, where supported.

commands.note: dirname operates on path strings and does not check for an existing directory.

commands.name: ln
commands.description: Creates symbolic or hard links to other filesystem entries.

options.description: Create a symbolic rather than a hard link.
Replace an existing destination if allowed; use carefully.

examples.description: Create a hard link on the same filesystem.

commands.note: Relative symbolic-link targets are resolved from the directory containing the link.

commands.name: stat
commands.description: Prints a file's size, permissions, timestamps, and other metadata.

options.description: Follow a symbolic link to its target where supported.
On GNU/Linux, choose an output format; %s prints size in bytes.

examples.description: On GNU/Linux, show file size in bytes.

commands.note: Formatting options differ between GNU/Linux and macOS; basic stat FILE is common to both.

commands.name: read
commands.description: Reads a line of input into one or more Bash variables.

options.description: Do not interpret backslashes as escapes; usually recommended.

examples.description: Read a line into the name variable.
Prompt for a name and save the answer.

commands.note: read is a Bash builtin. For example, printf '%s\n' "$name" displays the captured value.

commands.name: export
commands.description: Makes a shell variable available in the environments of programs started by the shell.

options.description: Stop exporting a variable without deleting its value.

commands.note: Exported variables last for the current shell and its child processes, not automatically for future sessions.

commands.name: env
commands.description: Displays environment variables or launches a command with temporary environment changes.

options.description: Remove a variable from the launched program's environment.

examples.description: Run date with a temporary language setting.

commands.note: Unlike export, env assignments before a command apply only to that command.

commands.name: sleep
commands.description: Waits for the given duration before continuing.

examples.description: Wait half a second if supported.

commands.note: Seconds are the default unit; some implementations also accept time suffixes.

commands.name: whoami
commands.description: Prints the effective user's name.
commands.note: For user and group IDs, use id.

commands.name: uname
commands.description: Prints kernel and machine architecture information.

options.description: Show the kernel or system name.

commands.note: uname does not necessarily report the distribution name or its user-friendly version.

commands.name: paste
commands.description: Merges corresponding lines from files, separated by a delimiter.

options.description: Use a comma as the field separator.
Join lines from each file into one long output line.

examples.description: Merge corresponding lines from two files.

commands.note: The default separator is a tab. Input lengths may differ.
